name: Pan-Seared Teriyaki Tofu Rice Bowls

components.name: Teriyaki Tofu

ingredients.name: Medium-firm tofu before pressing, from package
Potato or corn starch for dusting, some remains unused
Water, replacing sake and mirin for vegetarian alcohol-free adaptation
Brown sugar or maple syrup (nutrition modeled as sugar)

steps: Press tofu between clean towels under a weight for 20 minutes, then cut into even cubes.
Mix soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, water, ginger and garlic; this is an alcohol-free UNHANGRY teriyaki glaze, not Just One Cookbook's sake/mirin mixture.
Lightly dust tofu in starch, shaking off excess; pan fry in oil until crisp on both sides, 6-10 minutes total.
Pour in glaze and bubble briefly until glossy and clinging to tofu.
Pack tofu, rice and broccoli separately so tofu stays less soggy; serve extra sauce separately if possible.

components.name: Jasmine Rice & Broccoli
steps: Rinse rice and cook with measured water; rest covered 10 minutes. Steam broccoli until bright green and tender, then toss with sesame oil.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or within 1 hour if ambient temperatures exceed 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or colder for up to 3-4 days; freeze later-week portions promptly. If freshly prepared salad is included, prepare and store separately.
Reheat previously cooked leftovers to 74 C, stirring and checking the centre. For egg dishes, ensure eggs are completely set before portioning.
Cool cooked rice rapidly and keep refrigerated; avoid leaving rice at room temperature. Reheat rice thoroughly once.
Defrost frozen portions in the refrigerator. Re-crisp pastries, breaded vegetables and air-fried items in an oven or air fryer.
Keep delicate avocado, fresh salad, cold yogurt sauce and unbaked crisp toppings separate. They are generally not freezer-friendly.
Freezer designation describes likely quality, not independently established safety or shelf life.
